newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algerian troops kill 134 rebels in advance - report.
newsitem.headline: Algerian troops kill 134 rebels in advance - report.

text.p: Algerian troops backed by helicopter gunships have killed 134 Moslem rebels in attacks on their strongholds in west Algeria less than two weeks before a general election, a newspaper said on Tuesday.

The main Arabic language newspaper, Al Khabar, gave the toll as troops pushed forward on the fifth day of their advance towards a heavily fortified guerrilla base in the rugged El Gouassem area of Tissemsilt province.
It said guerrillas had meanwhile cut the throats of two civilians as they were travelling from northeastern Ksar Chellala to Algiers early on Sunday.
Another newspaper, Liberte, said a home-made bomb planted by rebels exploded near a motel in Draa Ben Khedda town, 90 kms (60 miles) east of Algiers, wounding five people on Monday.

The latest violence came one week before campaigning ends for the June 5 parliamentary election. More than 7,000 candidates are competing for 380 seats in the national assembly under the flags of 39 political parties or as independents.
Al Khabar said the troops advancing on the fortified El Gouassem rebel base had shot dead 120 rebels led by Ahmed Benaicha, deputy chief of the Islamic Salvation Army (AIS).

The newspaper, quoting local officials for the toll, said the rebels had carved out a reinforced concrete base under a mountain in the area straddling Ain Defla, Chlef, Relizane and Tissemsilt provinces and used it to train guerrillas.
Two guerrillas, who surrendered to authorities two weeks ago, tipped off the security forces about the base, it said.
On Monday, El Watan newspaper said government forces had killed more than 40 rebels and had more than 200 others trapped in El Gouassem area.
The two newspapers did not say whether Benaicha himself had been killed or was among those trapped as troops slowly advanced through the rugged terrain and mines planted by the rebels.

Security forces in a similar operation killed 11 guerrillas in Ben Ghazali mountain in the western province of Tlemcen and three others in two separate operations in the same province, Al Khabar added.
The authorities have made no statement on the reported operations and the newspapers did not say if there were any casualties among the government security forces.

The government, fighting Moslem rebels for the past five years, earlier offered residents 4.5 million dinars ($80,357) for information leading to the capture or death of Benaicha and AIS chief Madani Merzag, as well their rival, the Armed Islamic Group commander Antar Zouabri.
The AIS is the armed wing of the outlawed radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS).
Algerian security forces said last week they had killed four rebel leaders along with 13 guerrillas thanks to tip-offs from the public in return for rewards.

Residents in Algiers said posters put up on walls in several suburbs proposing rewards for information leading to the capture or death of Algeria's main rebel leaders were drawing more attention than posters of the parliamentary candidates.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence, which erupted in early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which FIS had taken a commanding lead.
